description: The concept revolves around a mission control and flight dynamics dashboard called "nCon". This system is designed to enable operators to control satellites efficiently and identify and resolve issues affecting spacecrafts by employing a highly customizable widget-based UI (User Interface) which is highly adaptable based on mission criteria and user preferences. These features are required to support a growing and evermore diverse satellite control operation. Operators will be able to easily customize each dashboard to their and mission-specific requirements. Instead of a rebuild in-house, changes can now just be made by mouseclicks. Furthermore, a plugin-based solution to enable the use of the most common event-streaming-pipelines is part of the project. The idea is primarily suited for MCC (Mission Control Center) operations, but the benefits extend to other domains as industrial operations.

description: The current manufacturing model for small satellites relies on distributed supply chains, multi-material assemblies, and sequential production steps, each adding cost, complexity and potential points of failure. Oniro S.r.l.’s Foam Additive Manufacturing (FAM) platform enables a new integrated production approach by combining structural fabrication and electronic embedding into a single automated process. By enabling the creation of composite structural components with localized material properties and the potential to embed PCB-based electronics directly within the build, Oniro's approach has the potential to reduce payload and part count, simplify assembly and cut production costs. This innovation offers a path toward scalable, cost-efficient, and robust manufacturing of small satellites.
